title: Repossession and Collateral Recovery Sale Period Computation
content:
**Standard period.** The standard sale period of a notice of intent to sell is 15 calendar days after its mailing date, that being the class minimum notice period in every collateral class of Repossession and Collateral Recovery. On the standard period, the base sale period is those 15 calendar days.

**Assembly.** The sale period is the base sale period plus every addition of days that applies, all in whole calendar days. The earliest sale date the notice states is its mailing date moved forward by the sale period.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical mailing date)

| Mailing date | Sale period | Earliest sale date stated |
|---|---|---|
| Monday 2 March 2026 | 15 calendar days | Tuesday 17 March 2026 |

The count runs in calendar days: weekends and holidays are counted like any other day, and the period is always a whole number of days.

## Basis Q&A

- *From which day is the period counted?* From the notice's own mailing date; the first day counted is the day after it.
- *Is the period expressed in business days?* No; the sale period is a count of whole calendar days.
